newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power softens on weather, restarts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power softens on weather, restarts.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were sharply lower Thursday as more nuclear power became available and temperatures rose, market sources said.

Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to climb to as much as 10-15 degrees F above normal by Saturday. Cooler weather is forecast to move in on Sunday, pushing temperatures to about three to eight degrees above normal.
Firm, peak power prices into Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) for Friday plummeted into the $16.00-17.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, down from Wednesday's trading at $28.00-29.50.
Firm, off-peak power prices into TVA were talked slightly lower in the $13.50-14.50 per MWh range, as TVA again began offering next-day power.
TVA's 1,170 MW Watts Bar nuclear power unit, in Spring City, Tenn., was in startup mode early this morning after shutting down late Monday.

At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak power prices in 16 hour blocks for Friday fell into the $19.50-20.50 range, down more than $4 from Wednesday, due to milder-than-expected weather and the anticipated return of some nuclear power.
Firm, off-peak power for Friday at the Ga./Fla. border was assessed at $13.00-14.00 per MWh.
Georgia Power's 741 MW Hatch 1 nuclear power unit remained shut but was expected to return to the grid Sunday or Monday.
Virginia Power's 781 MW Surry 1 nuclear power unit is also expected to be back on line early Saturday.
Also, Duke Power's 846 MW Oconee 2 nuclear unit, shut since last September after a steam pipe burst, will likely restart this weekend.
Oconee units 1 and 3, shut since October and each generating 846 MW, are expected to restart in February.
All three units are in Seneca, S.C.
